claims: A significant polar vortex split is expected in late March 2026.
The polar vortex split is likely to trigger a final, intense burst of cold air across the Upper Midwest and Northeast United States.
The disruption of the high-altitude, cold-trapping vortex will break the circulation into smaller, mobile cores.
The polar vortex split potentially causes temperatures 20-30°F below normal in some areas.
The polar vortex split is expected to impact weather patterns toward the end of March 2026.
The polar vortex split marks a final winter-like, late-season event.
Potential subzero lows in the Northern Plains.
Potential freezing temperatures extending into the South.
The active, cold pattern is expected to follow a "false spring" period.
The polar vortex usually keeps cold air confined to the Arctic.
The polar vortex will weaken and allow arctic air to move south.
The pattern shift is a result of a "final warming" event in the stratosphere.
The primary impact is forecast for the North-Central U.S. and Northeast.
Potential for cold air to affect portions of the East and Southeast.
The event represents a final, significant breakdown of the polar vortex for the 2025–2026 season.
